wording: SIM-MR-1 (no noise, no ALLD): ALLC, TFT and GTFT all score exactly 3.0 per round - without exploiters, conditionality confers no advantage (H4 supported).

SIM-MR-1 (5% execution noise, no ALLD): ALLC 2.872 >= GTFT 2.854 > TFT 2.727 - under errors and without exploiters, unconditional cooperation scored highest and strict reciprocity lowest (H5 supported).

SIM-MR-1 (5% noise): TFT-vs-TFT mutual cooperation fell to 0.278, while GTFT-vs-GTFT reached 0.767 - below the pre-registered 0.80, so H2 is Not supported, although the direction (forgiveness preserves cooperation under error) held.

wording: SIM-MR-1 replicator dynamics (5% noise, equal starts): ALLD fell to ~1e-5 and GTFT rose to 0.823, but ALLC persisted at 0.143 (TFT 0.033) - H3 (ALLC < 0.01) Not supported: once conditional strategies removed the exploiter, unconditional cooperators were no longer selected against.
counterevidence_limits: Finite-horizon Euler integration; well-mixed population; ALLC persistence may be neutral drift, not stability.

wording: Analogy (untested): if "unconditional love" is mapped to ALLC and "conditional love" to TFT/GTFT, the model suggests unconditional giving is costly only where exploiters persist and can coexist with forgiving conditional givers who limit exploitation. Nothing in SIM-MR-1 tests whether human love behaves like these strategies.
counterevidence_limits: Love is not a two-move game; no human data.

Ethical position of this report (per PLAN.md): "unconditional" regard or love must never be read as a duty to tolerate abuse; unconditional regard for a person is compatible with conditional access, boundaries, protection and justice.
counterevidence_limits: Normative stance; not an empirical finding.
